---
title: "Get Started"
---

This walkthrough builds, bundles, and installs a small module from nothing, then uses it from R. It assumes `carrier` is on your `PATH` (see [Installation](installation.qmd) if it isn't).

## 1. Scaffold a module

``` bash
carrier init rmod
```

This creates `rmod-proj/` (the default directory name is `<name>-proj`; override it with `--dir-name`):

```
rmod-proj/
├── carrier.toml
├── README.md
└── rmod/
    └── __init__.R
```

`carrier.toml` starts out mostly empty. Fill in `description`, `authors`, `license`, and any `[package_deps]` or `[module_deps]` your module needs. See the [carrier.toml reference](reference/carrier-toml.qmd) for the full schema.

The source directory (`rmod/`) is named after the module by default. If you'd rather use a different directory name, set `src` in `carrier.toml` (see [Module Structure](reference/module-structure.qmd)).

## 2. Write the module

Everything under `rmod/` is plain `{box}` code. `__init__.R` is the entry point, the module-level equivalent of `NAMESPACE`. Here's an example: 

``` r
#' @export
box::use(
    ./module1,
    ./module2,
)
```

## 3. Bundle it

From the project root:

``` bash
carrier bundle .
```

```
Bundled 'convert' (0.1.0) -> /path/to/rmod_0.1.0.tar.gz
```

Pass `--rmbx` to produce a `.rmbx` archive instead of `.tar.gz`. Either way, the archive embeds a `manifest.json` built from `carrier.toml` (see [Architecture](internals/architecture.qmd) for what goes into it).

## 4. Install it

From a local archive:

``` bash
carrier install rmod_0.1.0.tar.gz
```

Directly from a module directory (carrier bundles it to a temp file first, then installs that):

``` bash
carrier install .
```

Or from a GitHub repo, optionally pointing at a subpath:

``` bash
carrier install gh:username/path/to/rmod-proj
```

Installing prints where the module landed and the dependency plan carrier worked out from `[package_deps]` / `[module_deps]`:

```
Installed 'rmod' (0.1.0) -> ~/.carrier/modules/rmod
Dependencies:
  R packages:
    dplyr (*)
  Would install R packages (pass --install-deps to proceed):
    dplyr (*)
```

By default, R package dependencies are only *planned*, not installed. To install the main package dependencies, pass `--install-deps` to actually fetch and install them from CRAN (the default repo):

``` bash
carrier install rmod_0.1.0.tar.gz --install-deps
```

## 5. Use it from R

``` r
box::use(rmod)
rmod$module1$fn(...)
```

## 6. Remove it

``` bash
carrier remove rmod
```

You'll be asked to confirm; skip the prompt with `--force`.
